items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.summary: The article discusses how multimodal language models encode visual input, comparing pretrained vision encoders, training from scratch, and removing encoders, and examines design choices like visual prior, capacity, and fusion placement.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding these encoding strategies informs building more efficient, integrated vision-language AI systems.

items.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
items.summary: ArchSpace catalogs LLM architecture experiments, tracking successes, failures, and rationales to aid industry and academia in understanding scaling and efficiency.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers gain insight into effective architectural choices and cost trade‑offs for building large language models.

items.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
items.summary: The paper presents a neurosymbolic reinforcement learning framework that enforces investment policy constraints while optimizing portfolio allocation across market regimes.
items.whyItMatters: It enables compliant, AI-driven portfolio management, bridging regulatory rules and advanced RL performance.

items.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
items.summary: The paper explores whether machine learning engineering agents can use abundant unlabeled data to automate pipeline design when labeled data is scarce.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it could reduce data labeling costs and speed up deployment in real-world AI projects.

items.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
items.summary: The article explores how diffusion language models can identify and correct errors via remasking, revealing hidden state insights and limitations in Sudoku tests.
items.whyItMatters: It informs developers on improving model reliability and error correction strategies for advanced AI text generation.

items.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
items.summary: CoReMem lets coding agents store and retrieve edits from past tasks, balancing future benefit against write/read costs to aid successive coding on evolving repos.
items.whyItMatters: It improves efficiency for AI developers working on continuous integration and large codebases.

items.title: Linking Rapid Learning to Compositional Structure in Neural Networks: Evidence from Additive Analogies in Meta-Learned Parameter Spaces
items.summary: The paper explores how meta‑learning can endow neural networks with compositional structures that enable rapid learning of new functions from few examples.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it advances efficient AI, reducing data and training costs for real‑world applications.

items.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
items.summary: The paper introduces an efficient algorithm to estimate leave-one-out prompt attribution for language models, reducing evaluations from n to a constant factor under stability assumptions.
items.whyItMatters: It speeds up interpretability analysis, letting developers quickly pinpoint which prompt tokens most influence model outputs.

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.summary: Classical energy-based models learn reasoning tasks up to 1,000× faster than looped models, offering stability, fewer parameters, and adaptive compute.
items.whyItMatters: Faster, more efficient reasoning models mean quicker deployment and lower resource costs for AI developers.

items.title: Quantifying structural stability of transparent models for general insurance pricing
items.summary: The article discusses measuring how much insurance pricing models change after updates due to rapid data shifts.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because stable models reduce costly retraining and improve regulatory compliance.

items.title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate
items.summary: The article discusses a debate-based training protocol where humans judge competing models to improve alignment as capabilities grow.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a novel way to align complex models, potentially enhancing safety in advanced AI systems.

items.title: FLEX-LBP: Learning Local Binary Patterns with Exact Binary Inference for Texture Classification
items.summary: FLEX-LBP learns LBP parameters via backpropagation, computing exact binary codes and hard histogram counts for improved texture classification.
items.whyItMatters: It automates LBP tuning, boosting accuracy in industrial and medical imaging tasks.

items.title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
items.summary: Interactive video-to-video applications require real-time generation while maintaining long-range temporal consistency. However, recent methods achieve speed by restricting attention to a fixed-length causal window. This limits long-range consistency whenever relevant history falls outside the context window. items.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
items.summary: We investigate whether and how LLMs encode goals: internal neural representations that precede and guide action, and that are flexible enough to be realized through many different execution paths. We construct a coding setting with multiple sub-tasks that allows us to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and the selection of sub-goals. In this setting, we localize an encoding of the next sub-goal in…

items.title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
items.summary: On-device inference requires kernels that make effective use of local accelerators. Efficient training and evaluation of models that generate Apple Metal kernels benefit from native macOS tools and concurrent agent sessions. These sessions alternate between model requests, development commands, and GPU execution, leaving GPU capacity idle for much of a rollout. We present Metal Sandbox…

items.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically relies on a verifier that can reliably judge whether sampled solutions are correct. However, in many realistic settings, complete verification is generally unavailable, while cheap checks can only falsify failures. We formalize this regime as one-sided verifiability (OSV): verified negatives are reliable counterexamples, but verified…

items.title: Synthesis Smuggling: Maliciously Hiding Inferred Personal Attributes in LLM Outputs
items.summary: We propose Synthesis Smuggling, a novel threat model in which an adversarial LLM infers sensitive information about a user from routine assistance-seeking interactions and steganographically encodes that into innocuous-looking model-generated content. The user may then unknowingly transmit that information by sharing the generated artifact, say as an email, social-media post, or message, through…

items.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
items.summary: We introduce GeoWorld, a controllable and continuously evolving geographic environment platform for LLM agents, and LiveGeo, a benchmark for evaluating reliable decision-making in real-world geographic environments using GeoWorld. Unlike existing evaluations that largely reason and plan over fixed geographic states, GeoWorld is grounded in real-world geographic structure and allows external world…

items.title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated the ability to generate parameters for variational quantum circuits without conventional optimization. However, the conditions under which this approach is effective remain unclear. Here, we investigate a frozen, general-purpose LLM that generates complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions, with…

items.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
items.summary: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. A natural assumption is that more powerful and more expensive models consistently yield better heuristics.
